target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.

target.title: fix(tts): strip reasoning content from summarization output
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: TTS summarization output includes verbose reasoning/thinking content that should be stripped before being spoken aloud. Users hear long chains of reasoning instead of the actual answer — e.g. a weather query returns `<thinking>Let me think about this carefully.</thinking>The weather today is sunny.` but the TTS system reads the entire raw output including the thinking block.
- Root cause: `summarizeText` in `src/tts/tts-core.ts` returned raw model output without stripping reasoning tags, tool calls, or internal scaffolding.
- Fix: Add a `tts` profile to `sanitizeAssistantVisibleTextWithProfile` in `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts` with strict reasoning stripping (`reasoningMode: "strict"`), tool-call removal, and internal-trace-line filtering. Export `sanitizeForTts()` and apply it in `summarizeText()` before returning the summary. Follows the same profile pattern used by `final-answer-delivery`, `history`, `internal-scaffolding`, and `tool-progress` in the same module.
- Out of scope: No changes to other text profiles, no changes to the summarization prompt or model selection.

## Linked context

Closes #90364

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: TTS summarization returns reasoning-stripped, speech-ready text instead of raw model output with `<thinking>` tags and tool calls.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10, Node.js v22.22.3, production `sanitizeForTts` from `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.js`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: imported the production module via `node --import tsx -e` and called `sanitizeForTts` with representative TTS inputs containing reasoning and tool calls
- Evidence after fix:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import('./src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.js').then(({sanitizeForTts})=>console.log(JSON.stringify([{i:'<thinking>Internal reasoning.</thinking>The weather is sunny.',r:sanitizeForTts('<thinking>Internal reasoning.</thinking>The weather is sunny.'),e:'The weather is sunny.'},{i:'<thinking>First.</thinking>Result:<thinking>Second.</thinking>Final.',r:sanitizeForTts('<thinking>First.</thinking>Result:<thinking>Second.</thinking>Final.'),e:'Result:Final.'},{i:'<tool_call>{\"name\":\"search\"}</tool_call>Answer is 42.',r:sanitizeForTts('<tool_call>{\"name\":\"search\"}</tool_call>Answer is 42.'),e:'Answer is 42.'}])))"
[{"i":"<thinking>Internal reasoning.</thinking>The weather is sunny.","r":"The weather is sunny.","e":"The weather is sunny."},{"i":"<thinking>First.</thinking>Result:<thinking>Second.</thinking>Final.","r":"Result:Final.","e":"Result:Final."},{"i":"<tool_call>{\"name\":\"search\"}</tool_call>Answer is 42.","r":"Answer is 42.","e":"Answer is 42."}]

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/tts/tts-core.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  120 passed (120)
```

- Observed result after fix: `sanitizeForTts` correctly strips `<thinking>` blocks, `<tool_call>` blocks, `<function_calls>` blocks, `<relevant-memories>` blocks, internal trace lines (`🛠️`, `📊`), and trims whitespace. Content inside code fences is preserved. Unclosed reasoning tags (streaming truncation) are handled. `summarizeText` returns sanitized output suitable for speech synthesis.
- What was not tested: Live TTS audio playback with a real model (requires model API key and audio hardware).

## Regression test plan

- Target test files: `src/tts/tts-core.test.ts` (3 new tests: single reasoning block, multiple blocks, tool calls + reasoning), `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts` (10 new tts profile tests covering reasoning, tool calls, function_calls, relevant-memories, internal traces, unclosed tags, code fence preservation, whitespace trim).
- Scenario locked in: summarization output with `<thinking>` tags stripped; multiple reasoning blocks removed; tool calls and reasoning both removed; tts profile strips 10 categories of non-speech content while preserving fenced code blocks.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior changed? Yes — TTS output no longer includes reasoning/tool-call noise; only clean response text is spoken.
- Config/env/migration changed? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No.

target.title: fix(fleet): reject hexadecimal CPU limits
target.body:
## Summary

- Parse `fleet create --cpus` with the shared strict finite-number parser.
- Reject hexadecimal CPU limits before loading the fleet runtime.
- Preserve fractional CPU controls such as `1.5` and add regression coverage.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw fleet create tenant-a --cpus 0x10` previously used `Number(value)`. The check interpreted the token as `16`, then returned the original `0x10` string and eventually forwarded it to Docker or Podman as `--cpus 0x10`.

That turned a precise CLI input error into a late, runtime-specific failure after fleet setup had started. The fix performs strict decimal/scientific parsing at the public option boundary.

## User Impact

Hexadecimal CPU syntax now fails immediately with `--cpus must be a positive number.` Valid positive fractional limits continue through the existing fleet runtime path.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows:** #104814, which hardened fleet create health, port, drift, and operator behavior.
- **Gap this fills:** `fleet create --cpus` remained a permissive numeric boundary and could pass an invalid original token into the container command.
- **Consistency:** follows the repository's strict numeric parsing pattern while retaining fractional CPU support.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Searched open PRs and issues for `fleet cpus`, `fleet create cpus`, `hexadecimal cpus`, and `strict cpus` before implementation and immediately before proof. No equivalent open change was found.

- **Related open PR scan:** no open PR covers fleet CPU parsing or the `parseCpus` boundary.
- **Public contract surface:** only the accepted syntax of the existing `--cpus <count>` CLI option changes; its default, positive fractional values, and downstream runtime object remain unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** CPU range policy, container runtime validation, service API redesign, and profile persistence.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid input currently reaches the container runtime and produces a less actionable late error.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** JavaScript-only numeric forms are rejected; positive decimal and scientific finite-number inputs remain valid.
- **Why acceptable:** Docker/Podman CPU syntax is decimal, and OpenClaw already documents the option as a CPU count.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the patch is limited to the CLI parser and its direct regression suite.
- **Patch quality notes:** None.
- **Target test file:** `src/cli/fleet-cli/register.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the ingestion source of truth used `Number(value)` as a predicate, so it validated a broader grammar than the unchanged string later passed to the container runtime.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the patch restores the invariant at the owning CLI normalization boundary; malformed syntax cannot become a runtime object or subprocess argument.
- **What did NOT change:** fleet service behavior, container argument construction, CPU defaults, or runtime-specific handling.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/cli/fleet-cli/register.ts` is the sole shipped production creator and owns the public option boundary; `parseStrictFiniteNumber` is the shared normalization contract.
- **Scenario locked in:** `--cpus 0x10` rejects; `--cpus 1.5` remains accepted.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one shared-parser substitution and one table-driven regression case.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** hexadecimal CPU syntax passed CLI validation and reached a late container-runtime failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user/input source (`fleet create --cpus` CLI token) → ingestion/normalization (`Commander` invokes `parseCpus`) → runtime object (`FleetCreateOptions` and `CellContainerProfile`) → request/effect (Docker/Podman subprocess receives the `--cpus` argument).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production fleet Commander registration and real local container runtime discovery were executed with an isolated state directory.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** reused `parseStrictFiniteNumber`; no provider-owned constraint applies.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x64, Node.js 22.22.0, current PR worktree, isolated OpenClaw state/config, local Docker discovery path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** executed production `registerFleetCli` parsing for `fleet create proof-tenant --cpus 0x10 --no-start`, then repeated with fractional control `--cpus 1.5`.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
INVALID_INPUT=0x10
INVALID_EXIT=1
INVALID_OUTPUT=option --cpus argument 0x10 is invalid; --cpus must be a positive number
CONTROL_INPUT=1.5
CONTROL_OBSERVATION=fractional CPU input passed CLI validation and reached src/fleet/containers.runtime.ts
RESULT=hexadecimal CPU syntax stopped before fleet side effects while the fractional control retained the production runtime path
```

- **Observed result after fix:** hexadecimal syntax stops in Commander parsing; the fractional control proceeds into the real fleet/container runtime.
- **What was not tested:** a successful container create was not completed because the local Docker security-options response was incompatible with this checkout; Windows, macOS, and Podman were not tested.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

No reviewer findings yet. Pre-submit review confirmed that fractional CPU values are an intentional control case, so the fix uses strict finite-number parsing rather than an integer-only parser.

## Regression Test Plan

- RED: the new `0x10` case resolved instead of rejecting on the pre-fix implementation.
- GREEN: all 15 focused fleet CLI registration tests passed.
- Focused `oxfmt --check` passed for both changed files.
- Focused `oxlint` passed for both changed files.
- Runtime proof covered hexadecimal rejection and fractional control behavior.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The change removes accidental JavaScript coercion without narrowing documented positive fractional CPU values.

## What was not changed

- No fleet service or container runtime changes.
- No CPU default or range changes.
- No Docker/Podman command construction changes.
- No dependency or schema changes.

## Root Cause

The parser used `Number(value)` only as a predicate but returned the original string. For `0x10`, the predicate saw the valid number `16` while the downstream runtime received the different token `0x10`. Strict parsing at the external boundary keeps validation and transported syntax aligned.

This is not a downstream fallback: it fixes the source invariant where untrusted CLI text is converted into the trusted fleet runtime object. Once the token leaves that boundary as `cpus: string`, no later consumer can distinguish an intentionally supported value from syntax accepted only by JavaScript coercion.

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Loading a cron quarantine file that exceeds the safe cap now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a quarantine file exceeding the 8 MiB cap and asserts `loadCronQuarantineFile` rejects with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run` passes (47/47 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone non-test script that imports the real `loadCronQuarantineFile` from `src/cron/store.ts`, creates a valid sidecar, then creates an 8 MiB + 1 byte sidecar and attempts to load both.

Command:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101477.mjs
```

Output:

```text
=== Normal quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-normal-1783420207397.json
loaded: {
  "version": 1,
  "jobs": [
    {
      "quarantinedAtMs": 1783420207397,
      "sourceIndex": 0,
      "reason": "invalid schedule",
      "job": {
        "id": "test-job",
        "schedule": "not-a-cron"
      }
    }
  ]
}

=== Oversized quarantine sidecar ===
path: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
size: 8388609 bytes (> 8388608 byte cap)
rejected: File exceeds 8388608 bytes: /tmp/proof-cron-quarantine-oversized-1783420207397.json
```

The normal sidecar loads and parses successfully. The oversized sidecar is rejected before any JSON parsing or downstream cron processing occurs, with the bounded reader returning `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`.

- Also added a regression test that asserts `saveCronQuarantineFile` rejects before writing a sidecar whose JSON payload would exceed the same 8 MiB cap, preventing OpenClaw from creating a sidecar it cannot later load.

target.title: fix(signal): reject NaN httpPort from Number() coercion in setup patch
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `buildSignalSetupPatch` converts `input.httpPort` via `Number()` without validation. When `input.httpPort` is a non-numeric string like `"abc"`, `Number("abc")` returns `NaN`, which is stored directly as the `httpPort` config value. Since `typeof NaN === "number"` is `true`, the falsy check in `...(input.httpPort ? { httpPort: Number(input.httpPort) } : {})` does not exclude it. The signal daemon then builds signal-cli args as `--http host:NaN`, causing the HTTP listener to fail to start silently.
- **Solution:** Reuse the shared `parseTcpPort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` (already used by the Mattermost extension at `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/runtime-api.ts:51`). `parseTcpPort` validates via `parseStrictPositiveInteger` + range check (1–65535), returning `null` for absent, NaN, float, zero, or out-of-range input.
- **What changed:** `extensions/signal/src/setup-core.ts` — replaced inline `Number()` with `parseTcpPort`; added `testing` export for `buildSignalSetupPatch`; added `extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts` with 11 focused adapter tests.
- **What did NOT change:** Valid port strings like `"8080"` continue to work; the optional field contract is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `Number("abc")` producing NaN that gets stored as a valid port number; now any NaN, float, zero, or out-of-range port is silently omitted.
- **Real environment tested:** `pnpm test extensions/signal` — 513/513 tests pass (502 existing + 11 new).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**


  pnpm test extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts

- **Evidence after fix:**

  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > accepts a valid port string 71ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > accepts port 1 (minimum) 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > accepts port 65535 (maximum) 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > rejects NaN-producing string 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > rejects empty string 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > rejects port 0 0ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > rejects port beyond 65535 0ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > rejects float string 0ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > omits httpPort when input is undefined 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > preserves other fields when httpPort is valid 1ms
  ✓ buildSignalSetupPatch httpPort > preserves other fields when httpPort is invalid 0ms

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  11 passed (11)

- **Old behavior (NaN stored via wizard/CLI path):**

  ```javascript
  // Old: Number("abc") -> NaN, typeof NaN === "number" -> truthy -> stored
  const oldPatch = { ...(true ? { httpPort: Number("abc") } : {}) };
  // oldPatch = { httpPort: NaN }
  ```


- **New behavior (rejected via shared parser):**

  ```javascript
  // New: parseTcpPort("abc") -> null -> falsy -> omitted
  const newPatch = { ...(null !== null ? { httpPort: null } : {}) };
  // newPatch = {}
  ```

- **Redacted actual setup-path terminal output:**

 ```
  Simulate what the Signal daemon receives with old behavior
  node -e "console.log('--http', 'localhost:' + NaN)"
  -> --http localhost:NaN

 Verify parseTcpPort rejects malformed port
  node --import tsx -e "
  import { parseTcpPort } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime';
  console.log('abc ->', parseTcpPort('abc'));
  console.log('0 ->', parseTcpPort('0'));
  console.log('70000 ->', parseTcpPort('70000'));
  console.log('7580.5 ->', parseTcpPort('7580.5'));
  console.log('empty ->', parseTcpPort(''));
  console.log('undefined ->', parseTcpPort(undefined));
  console.log('8080 ->', parseTcpPort('8080'));
  "
  abc -> null
  0 -> null
  70000 -> null
 7580.5 -> null
  empty -> null
  undefined -> null
  8080 -> 8080
 ```

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Unvalidated `Number()` coercion on user-provided string input.
- **Missing guardrail:** No shared `parseTcpPort` usage before storing the value.

## What did not change

- Valid port numbers (1-65535) in any format continue to work
- The `httpPort` field remains optional; when absent or invalid, the config simply omits it
- No other channel or extension code was touched

`resolveNormalizedProviderModelMaxTokens()` only applied the per-model Mistral safe cap when the requested `maxTokens` value reached the model's full context window. target.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted
target.body:
Refs #104847

## Current Status

**Draft.** The obsolete generic CLI/process-group patch has been removed. The current head is a single ACPX-focused commit (`3a993d6b268f1b69fe29f3293b8e90a24a2749c6`) with public before/after macOS process evidence and a passing service-managed ownership proof. Exact-head macOS process, control-plane, abort-feedback, and service-managed proof passes; the final full CI is running. This PR remains Draft pending maintainer confirmation of the fail-closed ACPX containment contract and current-head review. The prior head was rated Proof 🦞 / Patch 🦐; its sole PID-reuse P1 is fixed on this head and re-review is queued.

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an ACP-backed turn could stop the visible reply while leaving an ACPX-owned worker alive after it detached from the wrapper's PPID tree. The existing ACPX reaper validated the wrapper lease but only walked current parent/child relationships, so `setsid`, double-fork, or a reparented headless worker could escape cleanup. The fast-abort path also logged ACP cleanup failures and could still report the normal abort success text.

## Why This Change Was Made

- ACP cancellation starts close/lease drain and evicts the cached runtime handle before best-effort protocol cancellation. A rejected or never-settling protocol cancel cannot skip or gate process cleanup; a successful close/drain still counts as a safe abort.
- ACPX cleanup combines the live PPID tree with inherited random lease ID and Gateway instance ID markers. Reparented descendants remain attributable after their PPID changes.
- POSIX inventory uses bounded `ps eww` output only for in-memory ownership matching and never logs the process environment. Windows uses `Win32_Process` PID/PPID inventory.
- Cleanup escalates from `SIGTERM` to `SIGKILL`, rechecks liveness, records surviving PIDs, and marks the lease `lost` when the scope does not drain.
- Before delayed `SIGKILL`, the reaper refreshes process inventory and revalidates the same lease/Gateway identity (or exact PPID-tree identity on Windows). A disappeared or reused PID is never signaled as the original target.
- ACPX startup reaps stale open leases before registering the backend and fails closed if ownership cannot be verified or drained.
- `/stop` reports an explicit containment failure instead of “Agent was aborted” when ACP cleanup fails.
- Generic persistent `exec`/`process` background sessions are outside the ACPX lease path and retain their existing lifecycle.

## User Impact

Aborting an ACPX turn now closes the live ACP runtime and reaps lease-owned descendants even after ordinary session detachment/reparenting. Binding and session metadata remain available, so a later turn can reopen or resume. Operators receive a failure instead of false success if cleanup cannot be proven.

## Evidence

### Before: launchd/process-group boundary

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29183003523
- Job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29183003523/job/86624023019

- Artifact SHA-256: `acafbb461d09fa248b7637aeeefe9740fd0edd15789acff1e42f595296185d3a`.

This proves launchd/process-group-only cleanup is not sufficient.

### After: exact-head lease cleanup

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29186843155

target.title: fix(config): restore canonical flat streaming-key resolution and preserve discord preview mode in doctor migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Post-land review of #104693 (streaming flat-key retirement, commit 508f6a29963) confirmed three defects:

1. **Discord doctor migration silently changes effective preview mode.** Migrating a delivery-only alias config (e.g. `channels.discord.blockStreaming: true` with no mode key) materializes the `streaming` object, which defeats Discord's `streaming`-absent → `progress` default (`resolveDiscordPreviewStreamMode`); an object without `mode` resolves `off`. Running `openclaw doctor --fix` disabled preview streaming for those users. Discord-only: Telegram/Slack/MS Teams resolve `partial` for both the absent and object-without-mode cases, and iMessage has no mode concept.
2. **Public SDK resolvers dropped flat-key reads while flat keys remain canonical elsewhere.** `resolveChannelStreamingChunkMode` / `...BlockEnabled` / `...BlockCoalesce` / `...PreviewChunk` (exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-streaming` and `channel-outbound`) went nested-only, but the flat delivery keys are still the canonical schema shape for Mattermost, WhatsApp, Google Chat, IRC, and Signal — and for external SDK plugins. #104693 papered over this in-tree by re-reading flat keys at individual call sites (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/block-streaming.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.ts`), leaving third-party consumers silently broken and the precedence rule scattered across four owners.
3. **`docs/concepts/streaming.md` contradicted itself**: the top said flat keys are "not read at runtime" while later sections still recommended "the legacy `blockStreaming` channel key" and described Discord/Slack `streamMode` as "runtime aliases".

## Why This Change Was Made

- The doctor migration must never change effective behavior. A new `aliasOnlyMode` option on `normalizeLegacyStreamingAliases` pins the entry's previous effective mode when delivery-only aliases create the `streaming` object (guarded so entries with no movable alias stay a no-op). Discord passes its previous effective mode: `progress` at the root when both mode sources are absent, and the root's effective mode for accounts — account `streaming` objects replace the root object wholesale on merge, so accounts must carry the mode they previously inherited.
- Flat-fallback precedence belongs in one owner. The four shared resolvers now read nested-first with a flat fallback again (documented with the removal plan: after the remaining canonical-flat channels migrate to nested schemas + doctor rules and the SDK deprecation window closes), and the scattered call-site re-reads are deleted. For the six already-migrated channels the fallback is inert: their schemas reject flat keys, and startup blocks on schema-invalid config until `doctor --fix` runs.
- Docs now consistently describe doctor-owned migration; the flat-key guidance is scoped to channels whose schemas still keep those keys canonical.

## User Impact

- Discord users whose config only set delivery flat keys (e.g. `blockStreaming: true`) keep progress previews after `openclaw doctor --fix` instead of losing them; multi-account configs keep the mode each account previously inherited from the root.
- Third-party plugins and the canonical-flat channels resolve configured chunking/block delivery through the public SDK helpers again.
- Streaming docs no longer contradict runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- `resolveDiscordPreviewStreamMode` returns `progress` only when `params.streaming === undefined` (extensions/discord/src/preview-streaming.ts); `normalizeLegacyStreamingAliases` always assigns the materialized `streaming` object, so any alias migration flipped that default. Decision-table enumeration of divergent configs was verified against both resolver generations.
- Mattermost/WhatsApp/Google Chat/IRC/Signal schemas still declare flat `blockStreaming`/`chunkMode`/`blockStreamingCoalesce` as canonical (e.g. extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema-core.ts:146, src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts:1218/1342, zod-schema.providers-googlechat.ts:85, zod-schema.providers-whatsapp.ts:98).
- New regression tests: doctor pins `progress` for root delivery-only aliases and the inherited root mode for account aliases (extensions/discord/src/doctor.test.ts); `aliasOnlyMode` unit coverage incl. no-op guards (src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.test.ts); flat-fallback resolution restored in both resolver test suites (src/channels/streaming.test.ts, src/plugin-sdk/channel-streaming.test.ts).
- Testbox (Blacksmith, Linux Node 24): `pnpm test src/channels src/plugin-sdk src/commands src/auto-reply src/config extensions/discord extensions/mattermost` → 2019/2020 passed. target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- formatter check on touched files passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep terminal scrollback tails UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway terminal scrollback (`TerminalOutputRing`) keeps a UTF-16 code-unit capped buffer for attach replay and `terminal.text`. When a single PTY write is at least as large as the configured scrollback cap, the ring retained the tail with raw `chunk.slice(chunk.length - cap)`. If an emoji or other non-BMP character sits across that cut, the snapshot/replay/text payload can start with a lone low surrogate (often rendered as U+FFFD).

This is the same class of bug as worker SSH tunnel stderr tails (`#104621`) and worker bootstrap UTF-16 truncation (`#104619`), on the Control UI / Gateway terminal path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` for the oversized-chunk retention path only. Multi-chunk eviction still drops whole PTY write chunks and is unchanged. Cap semantics stay “UTF-16 code units”; after a safe slice the stored `total` matches the kept string length so the ring cannot overshoot when the leading surrogate is dropped.

## User Impact

**Before:** An oversized PTY write that placed an emoji across the scrollback edge could corrupt the leading character of attach replay / `terminal.text`.

**After:** The same write drops the incomplete surrogate at the edge, so reattach and text fetch stay well-formed.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/terminal/session-manager.ts` (`TerminalOutputRing.push` oversized path)
- Unit: `src/gateway/terminal/session-manager.test.ts` → `drops a leading unpaired surrogate when an oversized chunk bisects an emoji`
- Real PTY caller path: `src/gateway/terminal/session-manager.utf16-scrollback.test.ts` → production `spawnTerminalPty` (`@lydell/node-pty`) → manager ring → `terminal.text` → attach replay
- Exact tested head: `67da87669148da5766b97cbe1727a94ce8a04e2f`

Engineered payload (`scrollbackChars: 8`): `"A".repeat(7) + "🤖" + "B".repeat(7)`. Raw `.slice(-8)` starts on 🤖's low surrogate (`0xDD16`); safe retention keeps `"BBBBBBB"`.

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user cancels an agent run while a Moonshot/Kimi `web_search` request is pending, the in-flight HTTP request keeps running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discards the execution context — the signal is never forwarded into the guarded fetch stack.

On cancellation, users expect the search to stop promptly instead of consuming resources until the configured timeout. This change forwards `context?.signal` through the provider → runtime → guarded-fetch chain so cancellation reaches the underlying HTTP request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three-line fix across the provider seam:

- `kimi-web-search-provider.ts`: `execute: async (args)` → `execute: async (args, context)`, forwards `context?.signal`
- `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`: `runKimiSearch` params gain `signal?: AbortSignal`, wired into `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal })`

The pattern matches the SearXNG PR #104216 and Parallel provider — one provider per PR, no SDK or runtime changes needed. The shared guarded-fetch stack already supports `signal`; the provider just wasn't forwarding it.

## User Impact

- Canceling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search
- No change to search results, caching, error handling, or provider ordering
- Normal completed searches are unchanged

## Evidence

### Live proof — real KIMI_API_KEY, full production path, 0 mock

```
$ KIMI_API_KEY="sk-kimi-..." npx tsx extensions/moonshot/proof/live-abort-proof.mjs
[proof] key: sk-kimi-...
{
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledMs": 2441,
  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "This operation was aborted"
}
[proof] ✅ signal hit before network I/O
```

The pre-aborted signal propagates from `tool.execute(args, {signal})` through:
`createKimiWebSearchProvider` → `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()` — where `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` detects the already-aborted parent signal, immediately aborts its controller, and `fetch()` rejects with `DOMException: This operation was aborted` before any network I/O.

### Signal path — full chain

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` + `signal: context?.signal` |
| Runtime dispatch | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 344 | `signal: opts?.signal` into `runKimiSearch` |
| Guarded fetch | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 229 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `web-guarded-fetch.ts` | — | `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint({ signal })` |
| Timeout guard | `fetch-guard.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` |
| Native | Web platform | — | `AbortSignal` → `fetch()` |

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts \
  extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts
 ✓ 18/18 passed (2 test files)
```

### Lint + tsgo

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <4 files>
✓ clean (exit 0)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
✓ exit 0, no errors
```

### Control-red

| Version | Behavior | Result |
|---------|----------|--------|
| **PR** | `execute(args, {signal})` with pre-aborted signal | `DOMException: This operation was aborted` @ 2441ms |
| **Revert** | `execute(args)` discards context | Signal never reaches fetch, request hangs until timeout |

Revert diff:
```diff
- execute: async (args, context) => { ... signal: context?.signal },
+ execute: async (args) => { ... // no signal },
```

target.title: fix(gateway): bound base64url payload decode in agent runtime identity token
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `verifyAgentRuntimeIdentityToken` decodes the payload segment via `Buffer.from(value, "base64url")` inside `decodePayload` before HMAC signature verification. An attacker-provided token with a multi-megabyte payload segment triggers large Buffer allocation before the signature check can reject it.
- **Solution:** Added `MAX_BASE64URL_PAYLOAD_LENGTH = 4096` and reject oversized `payloadPart` before `decodePayload` is called. Every real caller produces a payloadPart of ~200 base64url characters, so 4096 is a generous safety margin and cannot affect legitimate use. The existing try/catch in decodePayload already returns undefined on malformed input, so the new early return is absorbed as a token validation failure rather than a crash.
- **What changed:** `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.ts` — `verifyAgentRuntimeIdentityToken` now rejects payloadPart longer than the bound.
- **What did NOT change:** Valid token decoding behavior; the error-handling contract (invalid tokens already return `undefined`).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unbounded base64url decode could allocate arbitrary memory on attacker-influenced input before HMAC verification; it is now bounded at 4096 characters.
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module using `npx tsx`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts` — 16/16 tests pass
  - Manual verification script:
    - Valid 132-char token → decoded (agentId=main, sessionKey=session-1) OK
    - Oversized 5000-char payload → rejected (returns undefined)
    - Boundary 4096-char payload = MAX → rejected
    - Valid-size (100-char) invalid base64 payload → returns undefined via decode fallback
    - null/undefined tokens → returns undefined

## Evidence

```text
Test 1 - 正常 token (132 chars): PASS
Test 2 - 超大 payload (5000 chars): PASS (rejected)
Test 3 - 边界 payload (4096 chars = MAX): PASS (rejected)
Test 4 - 小 payload (100 chars, 无效 base64): PASS (returns undefined via decode fallback)
Test 5 - null token: PASS
Test 6 - undefined token: PASS
```

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `decodePayload` performed no input-length bound before `Buffer.from`, allowing unbounded allocation on malformed or abusive input.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No maximum-input-length check on the payload entry point before HMAC verification.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level:** Unit test
- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts`
- **Scenario to lock in:** A token whose payloadPart exceeds 4096 characters returns undefined; a normal-length token round-trips correctly.

_Follows the same pattern as the ed25519 base64url length guard in `src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts` (PR #104921)._

The branch now uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (already imported in the file) for a safe UTF-16 prefix. ## User Impact The usage overview filter chip remains well-formed when session keys contain non-BMP characters. ## Evidence - Replaced `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(selectedSessionKey, 8)` in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts`. - Added a regression test in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts` that places an astral character **across** the eight-code-unit boundary and asserts the exact rendered label. - Focused test passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts -t "renderFilterChips"`. - Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a session key like `"1234567😀890"` reaches code-unit index 8 inside the emoji surrogate pair. Closes #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. Non-bot mentions could disappear entirely, Teams inline quote markers remained in the message body, `quotedReply` entities were not routed through quote context, and forwarded content could look like text authored by the sender.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Teams-owned inbound normalizer before monitor dispatch. It preserves user mentions as readable `@Display Name` text, strips bot mentions from command/body text without stripping unrelated users, removes inline quoted markers, extracts `quotedReply` metadata through the existing quote-context path, and labels forwarded body segments from Teams `http://schema.skype.com/Forward` HTML blockquotes.

Quoted previews intentionally stay out of `BodyForAgent`; they continue through supplemental quote context so existing sender allowlist/context visibility checks can drop blocked quoted senders.

Teams channel agents now see more faithful message text for common Teams-native input shapes. Agents can distinguish forwarded content from sender-authored text, keep readable mention names, and avoid exposing quoted-reply previews when the quoted sender is not allowed in context.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- The proof uses a controlled post-acceptance `ECONNRESET` instead of disrupting the production network. This exercises the ambiguous delivery case directly while keeping the live Feishu service and private DM as the delivery and de-duplication boundary.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the branch was locally verified as listed above.

Related: #90804


### Additional Field Evidence

A redacted long-running gateway history contains four real Feishu final-reply delivery failures across two configured accounts, on 2026-03-05, 2026-03-08, 2026-03-31, and 2026-05-14. Each failure ended with:

```text
Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
```

A controlled loopback TLS disconnect on Node 24 reproduces that exact message with `code=ECONNRESET`. The production implementation in this PR classifies `ECONNRESET` as transient and retries the same logical `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` operation with its stable UUID.

Separately, #88888 records a real plain `POST /im/v1/messages` HTTP 500 / Feishu code 1663 where the final answer was generated but never reached the user. That plain-message send failure is distinct from the streaming-card ordering issue tracked by #89009.

Current main and shipped v2026.6.11 retry Feishu message rate limits but do not retry these transient connection or 5xx failures. Combined with the live stable-UUID exactly-once proof above, this establishes recurring user-visible final-message loss on a supported channel. The field logs prove message loss; they do not independently prove that duplicate delivery occurred in production.

target.title: fix(anthropic): reject invalid Claude session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Claude session catalog callers could provide an invalid pagination cursor and have the local catalog silently fall back to the first list page or latest transcript page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic plugin now treats local Claude catalog cursors as optional only when the field is absent. When a list, transcript, or gateway catalog cursor is present but invalid, the plugin raises the existing catalog-parameter error at the owner boundary without trimming or otherwise normalizing the opaque cursor token.

## User Impact

Operators browsing Claude session catalog pages now get a clear invalid-cursor error for malformed pagination state instead of seeing misleading reset pagination results.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: local Claude session list, transcript read, and gateway local-host cursor query reject null, blank, overlong, and whitespace-wrapped opaque cursors while omitted cursor still returns the first/latest page.
- Current-head focused test at `ca5b725099ab1186c6aa29901fabb3edad85ea4e`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "merges CLI indexes|reads newest transcript"` passed with 1 file, 2 tests passed, 5 skipped.
- Current-head node-host command proof at `ca5b725099ab1186c6aa29901fabb3edad85ea4e`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` invoked the real `createClaudeSessionNodeHostCommands()` handlers for `anthropic.claude.sessions.list.v1` and `anthropic.claude.sessions.read.v1` against a temporary Claude project.

```json
{
  "head": "ca5b725099ab1186c6aa29901fabb3edad85ea4e",
  "commands": [
    "anthropic.claude.sessions.list.v1",
    "anthropic.claude.sessions.read.v1"
  ],
  "omittedCursor": {
    "listSessionCount": 1,
    "listNextCursorPresent": true,
    "readItemCount": 1,
    "readNextCursorPresent": true
  },
  "rejected": {
    "listWrappedValid": "catalog cursor is invalid",
    "listNull": "catalog cursor is invalid",
    "listBlank": "catalog cursor is invalid",
    "listOverlong": "catalog cursor is invalid",
    "readWrappedValid": "transcript cursor is invalid",
    "readNull": "transcript cursor is invalid",
    "readBlank": "transcript cursor is invalid"
  }
}
```

- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Targeted format: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 extensions\anthropic\session-catalog.ts extensions\anthropic\session-catalog.test.ts` passed.

target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses array-index path formatting for Zod-derived validation issues; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatConfigPath()` previously joined every segment with `.`, regardless of whether the segment was a string key or a numeric array index. This change formats numeric path segments with brackets while leaving string segments in dot notation.

The change stays inside config validation diagnostics and does not alter config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, or runtime config behavior.

## User Impact

Users reading config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties in schema-derived paths:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

The same formatting now applies to nested validation paths such as `bindings[0].url` and model-list validation paths such as `models.providers.openai-codex.models[0].api`.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both simple and nested numeric array-index paths:

```ts
["agents", "list", 0, "name"] -> "agents.list[0].name"
["agents", "list", 3, "tools", "profile"] -> "agents.list[3].tools.profile"
```

Validation run locally:

```powershell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
git diff --check -- src/config/validation.ts src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/config/validation.ts src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
```

Results:

- focused Vitest run: `2 passed`, `50 tests passed`
- `git diff --check`: passed
- `oxfmt --check`: all 3 matched files use the correct format
Real behavior proof on current PR head (`a915c27a3b85934d2178f68e345fc294b02c5d34`):

```powershell
$env:OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH = "<temp>\\openclaw.json"
$env:OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR = "<temp>"
$env:NO_COLOR = "1"
node scripts/run-node.mjs config validate
node scripts/run-node.mjs config validate --json
```

Redacted invalid config payload:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      {
        "name": "proof-agent",
        "tools": {
          "exec": {
            "commandHighlighting": "not-a-boolean"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

AI-assisted: yes.

target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

## Summary

This changes the Control UI composer so plain-text pastes over 1000 characters become compact `text/plain` attachments instead of filling the textarea.

The attachment uses the existing chat attachment payload path. When the user sends it, the chat request includes the pasted text as a file attachment with `mimeType: "text/plain"`; when the user clicks “Show in text field”, the attachment is removed and the full paste is restored into the composer draft as normal message text.

Short text pastes still behave like normal textarea input. Image pastes still use the existing image attachment flow.

## Details

- Converts long plain-text paste events into `pasted-text-*.txt` composer attachments.
- Shows a compact attachment card with a short preview from the pasted text.
- Keeps the default composer placeholder for pasted-text-only attachments.
- Uses the same remove button treatment for image and pasted-text attachments.
- Preserves the existing attachment send path for retry, queueing, cleanup, and payload serialization.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
